classification.difficultyReason: Interpret depth as the opposite side and rope length as hypotenuse in the supplied triangle, then use inverse sine and round to minutes.

content.prompt:
A fishing boat is anchored in 65 m deep water. The anchor rope is 90 m long.
Calculate the angle the rope makes with the sea floor, to the nearest minute.

spec.description: Anchor at lower left, boat at upper right, horizontal sea floor and dashed vertical water depth. Two dedicated writing regions retain the rope and depth labelling task.
spec.mathematics: The rope is the hypotenuse; the water depth is opposite the angle at the anchor. The triangle is right-angled at the depth line's foot.
spec.answerVisibility: Only theta and Sea floor are supplied. Both measurement boxes are empty.

answer.worked:
Label the rope $90\text{ m}$ and the vertical depth $65\text{ m}$.
$$\begin{aligned}\sin\theta&=\frac{65}{90}\\\theta&=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{65}{90}\right)\\\theta&\approx46.2383^{\circ}\\\theta&\approx46^{\circ}14'\end{aligned}$$
The fractional degree is approximately $14.30'$.

spec.description: Completed mathematical triangle with rope and depth labels.
spec.mathematics: Hypotenuse 90 m and opposite side 65 m.
